problem: Existing explainability methods like GAMs and SHAP rely on additive decompositions that lose information through signal cancellation when features have strong interactions.
approach: Tensor Separation Learning learns a sum of rank-1 products of univariate functions via stagewise greedy procedure, enforcing separability to preserve higher-order interactions.
contribution: TSL can be fully reconstructed from first-order partial dependence functions and competes with black-box models on regression benchmarks without information loss from additive projections.

problem: Multimodal Graph Foundation Models fail to explicitly model cross-modal interactions and lack proper modality alignment needed to capture semantic relationships across different modalities.
approach: PLANET uses divide-and-conquer with Embedding-wise Domain Gating for local semantic enrichment and Node-wise Discretization Retrieval for global modality alignment across multiple granularities.
contribution: PLANET significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on diverse graph-centric and multimodal generative tasks through explicit modality interaction and alignment.

problem: Multimodal language models process long-form clinical videos with passive sampling and weak grounding, limiting ability to iteratively locate and verify predictions with temporal evidence.
approach: MedScope performs coarse-to-fine evidence seeking with tool calls and verification, optimized via GA-GRPO that reinforces tool use with grounding-aligned rewards.
contribution: MedScope achieves state-of-the-art on video understanding benchmarks with predictions explicitly grounded in temporally localized visual evidence.

problem: Lack of unified understanding of which modeling choices drive improved brain alignment across diverse neural recording modalities and datasets.
approach: Systematically investigates scaling laws across 8 neural datasets and 600+ models, examining pretraining, fine-tuning, and mapping effects; proposes novel subject-shared cross-attention mapping.
contribution: Establishes multimodal scaling laws showing pretraining saturation, complementary fine-tuning benefits, and log-linear mapping gains that generalize across recording modalities.

problem: LLM-based agents perform well on benchmarks but fail in real-world deployments with noise and stochasticity, due to evaluation built on idealized assumptions.
approach: AgentNoiseBench injects controllable user-noise and tool-noise into existing benchmarks while preserving task solvability, then evaluates diverse models across noise conditions.
contribution: Reveals consistent performance variations and sensitivity of current agentic models to realistic environmental perturbations through systematic evaluation.

problem: Standard 2D rotary position embedding in vision transformers restricts to axis-aligned directions, hindering modeling of oblique spatial relationships in natural images.
approach: Spiral RoPE partitions embedding channels into multiple groups with uniformly distributed directions, rotating each group by position projection onto its direction.
contribution: Spiral RoPE consistently improves performance on classification, segmentation, and generation with better attention to semantically relevant objects and object boundaries.

problem: Diffusion language models suffer from pretrain-to-posttrain mismatch between masked training and real causal inference, limiting speedup or degrading performance.
approach: Jacobi Forcing directly post-trains causal multi-token predictor from autoregressive LLM via progressive distillation based on model's own token generation trajectories.
contribution: Achieves 3.8× wall-clock speedup with minimal performance loss and up to 4.6× token acceptance rate improvement through multi-block decoding with rejection recycling.

problem: Unclear how batch size, momentum, and variance reduction interact to determine the implicit bias and convergence of stochastic steepest descent in multi-class classification.
approach: Characterizes implicit bias of mini-batch stochastic steepest descent under general entry-wise and Schatten-p norms, analyzing batch-momentum trade-offs and variance reduction.
contribution: Shows momentum enables small-batch convergence to max-margin solutions and variance reduction recovers exact full-batch bias with explicit dimension-free convergence rates.

problem: Deep multi-view clustering fails to model data uncertainty and forces high-quality views toward corrupted ones due to reliance on flat Euclidean embeddings.
approach: HAMC maps features into Poincaré ball with radial geometry as confidence proxy, uses asymmetric view alignment for reliable-to-unreliable guidance, and consensus-aware cluster learning.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on multi-view clustering through uncertainty-aware hyperbolic embeddings and confidence-based screening.

problem: Geometry remains fragmented in formal reasoning with domain-specific languages lacking formal guarantees, while existing Lean geometry efforts use incompatible axiom systems and insufficient scale.
approach: Euclean automatically formalizes geometry in native Mathlib through constraint explication, configuration anchoring, formalization mapping, and iterative repair.
contribution: Constructs OMNI-Geometry (768 problems) and Numina-Geometry (177,597 problems), the largest Lean geometry datasets; improves proof success from 13.6% to 15.1%.

problem: Lack of approximation-theoretic guarantees for Transformer architectures that enforce Lipschitz continuity, limiting their use in safety-critical applications.
approach: Proposes gradient-descent-type in-context Transformers that are Lipschitz-continuous by construction via MLP and attention blocks as Euler steps of negative gradient flows.
contribution: Proves universal approximation theorem for Lipschitz-constrained Transformers with approximation guarantees independent of token count using measure-theoretic formalism.

problem: Diffusion models for tabular anomaly detection require multi-step noise schedules with significant computational complexity.
approach: Uses fixed-noise denoising without generation target, employs self-supervised preconditioning with explicit linear reference channel, derives anomaly score from expected deviation under perturbations.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on ADBench with 1.22% AUCROC and 1.13% AUCPR improvement through single-step stability-based objective.

problem: Existing UED methods evaluate environments using indirect proxy signals (regret, value errors) with high bias, variance, or computational overhead.
approach: PACE scores levels by squared ℓ2 norm of parameter change from provisional policy update, guiding level selection via staleness-aware buffer and rank-based prioritization.
contribution: Consistently outperforms established UED baselines in zero-shot generalization across diverse evaluation protocols through low-variance parameter-change scoring.

problem: Classical data assimilation methods rely on Gaussian approximations violated for complex dynamics or observation operators, limiting probabilistic inference.
approach: DAISI combines flow-based generative priors with inverse-sampling step to incorporate forecast information, then assimilates observations via guidance-based conditional sampling.
contribution: Achieves accurate filtering in nonlinear regimes with sparse and noisy observations where traditional methods struggle without retraining the prior at each step.

problem: Audio self-supervised learning relies on generative objectives; contrastive approaches underexplored due to high augmentation design cost and large batch requirements.
approach: AudioMosaic applies time-frequency masking to spectrogram patches as augmentation, enabling efficient contrastive learning with reduced computational cost.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on audio benchmarks with strong transferability across datasets and domains; enhances LLMs when integrated for audio perception.

problem: Flow-based generative models struggle to enforce strict safety constraints in physical systems, with post-hoc corrections causing computational overhead and distribution distortion.
approach: PolyFlow embeds polytope constraints directly into flow dynamics using discrete-time formulation and projection-free architecture with Euler steps.
contribution: Achieves zero constraint violation while maintaining distributional fidelity with significantly reduced inference latency versus constrained generation baselines.

problem: Robustness certification frameworks study geometric transformations but lack methods for certifying VLM robustness under semantic-level variations.
approach: Uses text prompts as semantic proxies to construct transformations parameterized by extent, characterizes VLM decision boundary in closed form to certify robustness intervals.
contribution: First framework certifying VLM robustness under semantic variations without requiring additional data per variation; validates across synthetic and real-world data.

problem: Discrete neural samplers suffer from mode collapse and fail to explore high-energy barrier regions critical for free energy estimation.
approach: MetaDNS integrates well-tempered metadynamics into discrete diffusion/autoregressive samplers with adaptive history-dependent bias potential.
contribution: Enables free energy reconstruction and explores inaccessible regions on low-temperature benchmarks (Ising, Potts, copper-gold), comparable to MCMC-based metadynamics.

problem: Post-hoc model merging suffers from task interference and information erasure when combining multiple task-specialized language models.
approach: METIS employs iterative many-shot merging with task-wise loss-gap weighting and consensus-based masking to mitigate interference.
contribution: Improves multi-task performance with significant gains on worst-performing tasks, effectively mitigating information erasure across task-specific models.

problem: Tensor Product Representations suffer exponential dimensionality growth for deep structures while Vector Symbolic Architectures sacrifice capacity through noisy compression.
approach: Orthogonal Subspace Carving projects fillers onto null space of role basis before aggregating into fixed order-p tensor, enforcing geometric orthogonality.
contribution: Decouples tensor order from structural depth, enabling deep recursive binding within constant memory footprint with orders of magnitude smaller component vectors.

problem: Lifelong model editing suffers from catastrophic forgetting and model collapse; the mechanism of Lifelong Normalization's stability remains unclear.
approach: Analyzes Lifelong Normalization in lifelong regime, showing it yields asymptotic orthogonality and bounded parameter norms; proposes StableEdit with warm-up and whitening.
contribution: Provides first theoretical account of Lifelong Normalization; StableEdit improves long-horizon stability with competitive performance at minimal computational overhead.

problem: Disentangled representation learning overlooks hidden correlations where data under certain attributes exhibit underlying modes correlated with other attributes.
approach: CoDID jointly discovers modes and enforces mode-based conditional independence via dynamic architecture with meta-optimization coordination mechanism.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on disentanglement tasks by mitigating error amplification in iterative mode discovery.

problem: Masked Diffusion Models performance depends crucially on inference-time unmasking order; confidence-based sampling is myopic and cascades early errors.
approach: LookUM guides sampling with verifier over unmasking paths using importance sampling; couples path generator proposing unmasking sets with uncertainty-aware path selection.
contribution: Validates on six benchmarks (math, planning, coding) with consistent improvements; LLaDA with LookUM matches RL-tuned performance and yields additional gains.

problem: Deterministic climate models fail to capture uncertainty; existing generative approaches oversimplify by neglecting spatiotemporal dependencies and cross-scale interactions.
approach: ClimateAR is autoregressive generative model with aligned tokenizer bridging simulation/real-world data and mixed-scale conditioning for multi-scale interactions.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art with 37.56% average anomaly correlation improvement over leading baselines on seasonal-to-interannual forecasting.

problem: Existing privacy definitions lack game-theoretic grounding or are disconnected from practical guarantee assessment.
approach: Proposes framework measuring privacy from Bayesian game-theoretic perspective, enabling purpose-driven privacy definitions with rigorous justification.
contribution: Shows pure and probabilistic differential privacy are special cases; provides new interpretations of post-processing inequality and enables deterministic algorithm privacy.

problem: Transformer expressivity results rely on unrealistic hardmax attention and high precision, disconnecting from practical models.
approach: Analyzes standard transformers with softmax, rounding, and logarithmic depth/width; constructs hardmax with ternary activations simulating Turing machines via CoT.
contribution: Converts to softmax equivalents; analyzes summarized CoT simulating Turing machines more efficiently; empirically validates on Sudoku reasoning.

problem: Robust conformal prediction with randomized smoothing requires expensive Monte Carlo sampling at both calibration and test time to balance prediction set size.
approach: Front-Loaded RCP increases sampling at calibration (one-time preprocessing) while keeping test-time sampling low, exploiting that calibration can absorb higher overhead.
contribution: Matches state-of-the-art test-time complexity while producing considerably smaller prediction sets at larger perturbation radii.

problem: Lack of statistical theory explaining when masked corruption outperforms alternatives in discrete diffusion for language generation.
approach: Establishes generalization bounds across different forward corruption kernels, revealing masking scales with effective data support rather than full state space.
contribution: Shows masking mitigates curse of state space cardinality; structure-aware refinements capture concentration and sparsity benefits in sequential data.

problem: Neural combinatorial optimization solvers learn narrow tasks and struggle with diverse problem distributions lacking generalization capabilities.
approach: M²GenCO formulates problem types as tasks in meta-learning framework, uses diffusion-based solving with lightweight GNN for joint pre-training and fine-tuning.
contribution: Achieves 9.16% performance gain with 95.6× inference acceleration; state-of-the-art on all test sets; 82% and 91% savings in training resources and time.

problem: Multi-view 3D human pose estimation for multiple individuals is limited by synthetic data domain shift and assignment problem complexity.
approach: DisPOSE frames multi-person assignment as diffusion over polystochastic tensors with differentiable Sinkhorn projections; regresses skeletons via Hypergraph-Convolutional Decoder.
contribution: Outperforms self-supervised methods; demonstrates high label efficiency retaining 99% performance with 10% pseudo-labels; robust on occluded surgical scenes.

problem: Defocus deblurring in pathology microscopy has spatially varying and discontinuous blur that violates shift-invariance assumptions of deep learning methods.
approach: DGNO parameterizes integral kernel via discontinuous Galerkin formulation with element-local volume operators and interface numerical fluxes.
contribution: Surpasses state-of-the-art with sharper reconstructions, robust spatially varying blur handling, and scalable high-resolution performance.

problem: Multi-bit LLM watermarking lacks selective disclosure control, requiring full message revelation for partial verification and raising privacy concerns.
approach: HeRo recursively partitions vocabulary across hierarchical layers, distributing watermark information so different verifiers access only permitted portions.
contribution: Enables selective disclosure with fine-grained access control while preserving text quality unbiasedness and achieving high detection accuracy with low latency.

problem: Parameter sharing in MARL struggles in heterogeneous environments with diverse agent capabilities; customized policies reduce knowledge transfer efficiency.
approach: Dspic uses self-supervised learning for discriminative role embeddings with complete observation space division guarantee; incorporates diffusion policy for complex action distributions.
contribution: Achieves superior sample efficiency while maintaining asymptotic optimality across MaMuJoCo, SMAC, SMACv2, and LBF benchmarks.

problem: Discovery of randomized linear algebra algorithms remains manual, requiring deep expert knowledge; RL struggles with sparse rewards and vast search spaces.
approach: RL4RLA builds explicit algorithms from linear algebra primitives; uses numerical curriculum for inductive bias and Monte Carlo Graph Search for exploration.
contribution: Rediscovers state-of-the-art methods (sketch-and-precondition, Randomized Kaczmarz, Newton Sketch) optimized for accuracy/speed/stability trade-offs.

problem: Gaussian processes are limited by handcrafted kernel functions requiring expert knowledge and imposing strong assumptions on hypothesis space.
approach: Empirical GPs estimate mean and covariance functions from historical data corpus as hierarchical Bayesian prior; derives EM algorithm for learning from multiple datasets.
contribution: Converges to KL-divergence closest GP to real distribution; achieves competitive performance on learning curve extrapolation and time series forecasting.

problem: Compositional generalization to unseen goals under novel contexts is limited by trajectory stitching over contiguous segments in offline goal-conditioned RL.
approach: Formalizes analogy transduction composing task-endogenous analogies with contexts; proposes analogy representation capturing optimal execution changes invariant to variations.
contribution: Enables transduction beyond seen analogy-context pairs; substantially outperforms prior methods on OGBench manipulation without analogy transduction.

problem: Existing formal mathematics benchmarks focus on isolated theorem proving without evaluating repository-scale proof engineering requiring multi-file coordination.
approach: APE framework extracts proof engineering tasks from real library commit histories; introduces APE-Agent alongside Claude Code and Codex for standardized comparison.
contribution: First systematic framework evaluating repository-scale proof engineering with contract-based design enabling fair comparison across diverse formal mathematics tasks.

problem: Graph domain adaptation lacks explicit treatment of cross-domain node-level homophily mismatch limiting transfer effectiveness.
approach: PSAHS reweights edges and adds intra-class connections to enhance source homophily; conservatively refines target graph; alternates structure adjustment with domain-adversarial alignment.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines with particularly large gains under severe homophily mismatch, highlighting importance of explicit homophily alignment.

problem: Policy-gradient training instability and slowdown as learning progresses; understanding noise-to-signal ratio evolution lacks characterization.
approach: Characterizes noise-to-signal ratio for linear systems and polynomial systems in closed form; derives upper bound for general nonlinear dynamics.
contribution: Shows NSR landscape is highly non-uniform and typically increases approaching optimum; NSR can blow up triggering instability, explaining training collapse phenomena.

problem: Norm-minimizing interpolators in Sobolev spaces show benign overfitting in some settings but harmful in others; theoretical understanding incomplete.
approach: Studies generalization of functions in W^{k,p}(ℝ^d) perfectly fitting noisy training data; uses geometric argument identifying harmful neighborhoods via Sobolev inequalities.
contribution: Proves harmful overfitting for arbitrary p ∈ [1,∞) under label noise and sufficient regularity; generalization error bounded below by positive constant.
